subject: Clearsky Finance – in-region processing, fallback behavior & deletion evidence
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@clearsky-finance.eu>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal - Clearsky <legal@clearsky-finance.eu>, Marco Alvarez <marco.alvarez@clearsky-finance.eu>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:14:00+01:00
Subject: RE: In-region processing questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. We are evaluating Redwood for a pilot and need explicit confirmation on a few points before we proceed to procurement and Legal: 

1) Can you confirm that Clearsky customer data can be processed and stored only within EU jurisdictions (we are looking specifically at Germany/Netherlands regions)? Do you ever route requests outside the EU for inference or storage under the default Hosted API?

2) If a capacity or latency incident occurs in-region, what is your fallback behavior? Can we require an EU-only policy that prevents any cross-border failover?

3) Deletion & retention: we need a deletion SLA and a sample proof-of-deletion artifact for active data and backups (we need to show auditors how deletion is verified).

4) Contractual: we will require SCCs and any supplementary measures you rely on. Please provide the latest SCC addendum, the data flow diagram showing all subprocessors, and a sample deletion evidence file. Also state whether customer-managed KMS is available.

Can you send a single response with attachments and proposed contractual language we can pass to Legal?

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Privacy, Clearsky Finance

Attachments requested: SCC addendum, data flow diagram, deletion evidence sample
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Can each of you weigh in on your area and I will consolidate:

- Kimberly: proposed contractual/wording for SCCs + any recommended supplementary measures and a suggested deletion SLA (active vs backup).
- Markus: ops/SRE checklist for how we would enforce an EU-only policy and monitoring/audit evidence we can provide.

We should aim to send Clearsky a consolidated reply tomorrow.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of EU Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-01T11:27:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clearsky questions – need confirm & materials

Hannah — quick technical summary (for the customer reply):

- In-region processing: For the Hosted product we have EU regions (Frankfurt, Zfcrich, and Amsterdam depending on customer location). By default requests from EU accounts are routed to EU regions. We do not replicate customer request payloads to non-EU regions unless a configured fallback or routing policy requires it.

- EU-only enforcement: We support an EU-only routing policy that prevents any active cross-border failover for an account. This is enforced at the routing-control plane and at the orchestration layer; we can pin model variants and capacity to EU pools.

- Fallbacks: There are two fallback behaviors we can offer: (a) soft-fail (request queued/rejected when EU capacity is exceeded) or (b) explicit cross-border fallback (only if customer enables it). For Clearsky we can set default to soft-fail unless they opt into spillover.

- KMS/keys: Customer-managed KMS is available for Private deployments and Dedicated (bring-your-own-key supported via KMS integration). For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with keys managed by Redwood; we can evaluate customer-specific KMS for enterprise contracts.

- Backups & deletion: Active inference state and model KV caches are ephemeral and deleted per config (typically immediately after session TTL). Request logs and audit logs are retained per our retention policy (we can shorten to meet contractual needs). Backups (snapshot & object store) are stored in-region by default. We have a documented backup purge workflow; after a deletion request we mark data for purge and run an in-region purge job — typical completion window is 30 days for active containers and up to 90 days for object-store snapshots (we can tighten this in an addendum).

- Evidence: We can produce a sample deletion-evidence CSV (example fields: object_key, deletion_time, purge_job_id, region, operator_id) and provide activity logs with trace ids.

I attached the EU data-flow diagram (eu-data-flow-diagram.png) and an example deletion evidence CSV (deletion-evidence-sample.csv).

If we want to offer the strongest guarantee, recommend: EU-only routing policy + Dedicated capacity or Private deployment + Customer-managed KMS.

-Rishi
Sr. Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: eu-data-flow-diagram.png (PNG), deletion-evidence-sample.csv (CSV)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-01T14:40:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clearsky questions – need confirm & materials

Hannah/Rishi — legal commentary and suggested language: 

1) SCCs & addendum: We maintain an SCCs addendum compatible with the latest EU Commission set (we will provide the current addendum). The addendum includes: subprocessors list, in-region processing commitments, and a clause confirming that cross-border transfers will not occur absent explicit customer authorization.

2) Supplementary measures we recommend including in the DPA:
- Mandatory in-transit and at-rest encryption (TLS + provider SSE)
- Contractual obligation for Redwood to maintain EU-only processing for the account and to provide notification & pause/soft-fail options in case of capacity events
- Customer audit rights and regular compliance evidence (SOC 2 report, CSV deletion evidence, and audit log extracts)

3) Deletion SLA (suggested):
- Active stored customer data: purge within 30 days of written request; evidence provided within 5 business days of purge completion.
- Backups/object-store snapshots: purge within 90 days; if customer requires shorter window we can propose 60 or 30 days for Dedicated/Private.

4) Contract language snippet (for DPA):
"Redwood Inference shall process and store Customer Data solely within the jurisdictions of the European Union as specified in the Order Form unless the Customer expressly authorizes cross-border processing in writing. In the event of capacity constraints, Redwood shall (i) notify the Customer and (ii) implement the Customer's selected fallback policy (EU-only soft-fail or explicit cross-border spillover)."

I have prepared the SCCs addendum (redwood_sccs-addendum-v2.pdf) with the recommended supplementary measures highlighted. I recommend we offer Clearsky: EU-only routing + option to upgrade to Dedicated or Private to get a 30-day backup purge SLA and customer-managed KMS.

-Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy

Attachments: redwood_sccs-addendum-v2.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-02T15:02:00+01:00
Subject: RE: Clearsky Finance – in-region processing, fallback behavior & deletion evidence

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Sending consolidated answers and the materials we discussed. Please find attached:
- redwood_sccs-addendum-v2.pdf (SCC addendum with supplementary measures called out)
- eu-data-flow-diagram.png (high-level subprocessors & data flow)
- deletion-evidence-sample.csv (example proof-of-deletion format)

Summary answers:
- In-region processing: We can enforce EU-only processing and storage for your account (Frankfurt/Amsterdam). By default Hosted routes EU accounts to EU regions. We will not route data outside the EU unless you expressly authorize spillover.
- Fallbacks: We will configure Clearsky to soft-fail / queue when EU capacity is constrained. Cross-border spillover will only occur if you opt in.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys are available on Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we can discuss a managed key arrangement for enterprise customers.
- Deletion SLA: Proposed (per Kimberly) — active data purged within 30 days; backups purged within 90 days (we can offer 30/60 on Dedicated). Deletion evidence will be provided in a CSV with object ids, timestamps, purge job ids, and trace ids.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached addendum and let us know whether your Legal is happy with the supplementary measures and SLA.
2) If Legal approves, sign the addendum via DocuSign: https://docusign.com/CLSFY/Redwood-SCCs-Addendum/xyz
3) If you want the strongest operational guarantee, we recommend starting the pilot on Dedicated capacity (we can provide pricing/commitments) or using our Private offering for full KMS control.

If helpful, we can schedule a short 30-minute call next week with Rishi and Kimberly to walk Legal and Engineering through the diagram and deletion evidence.

Thanks and speak soon —
Hannah
